rationale: Top ranked in Tier 1 for its strong fit with the DHHS plan and a large award (about $7.5M, estimated), funding statewide viral hepatitis surveillance, outbreak response and testing-to-care work that the state health department already runs.

Ranked high for the largest Tier 1 award (up to about $22M) and strong help per person, funding comprehensive preventive and primary care for medically underserved communities through the Health Center Program; confirm DHHS can be the applicant for NC's service areas.

A second Health Center Program Service Area Competition (up to about $19.2M), ranked for its award size and help per person, funding preventive and primary care in medically underserved service areas.

Ranked for a large award (up to $22M) and strong help per person, building a network of hospitals, nursing homes and public health partners to detect, respond to and prevent threats to patient and health-worker safety.

The third Health Center Program Service Area Competition (up to about $15.3M, due Jan 8, 2027), ranked for award size and help per person, supporting preventive and primary care for underserved communities.
Ranked for a sizable award (up to $9M) that supplements NC's existing Ryan White Part B and AIDS Drug Assistance Program formula funding, so it builds on a program DHHS already runs.
Ranked for its award (about $8.5M, estimated) and statewide reach, funding health-department work to track, prevent and control syphilis, gonorrhea and chlamydia.
Earns most of its points from a large estimated award (about $41M), funding surveys plus expanded infectious disease testing, treatment and prevention in settings that serve people who use drugs.

Ranked for high help per person (about $20 per uninsured North Carolinian) and a large estimated award (about $21.7M), funding the state's system of HIV care and treatment for low-income people with HIV.

Ranked for a $10M award and strong help per person, providing emergency funds to prevent or eliminate AIDS Drug Assistance Program waiting lists and shortfalls; due Nov 2, 2026, the earliest Tier 1 deadline.
Ranked for its award (up to about $5.1M) and help per child, supporting standardized fetal, infant and child death reviews whose findings shape local prevention strategies.
Ranked for its award (about $2.75M, estimated) and statewide reach, strengthening stillbirth and birth-defect surveillance and research into their still-unknown causes.
Ranked for its award (about $3M, estimated) and statewide reach, funding a whole-person wellness approach to STI prevention that helps people make healthy choices and build healthy relationships.
Ranked for its award (about $2.2M, estimated) and statewide reach, linking maternal-child surveillance on alcohol use in pregnancy, neonatal abstinence syndrome and CMV to partner action.
Ranked for statewide reach and a $1.14M award, funding active surveillance of children's respiratory and stomach illnesses and how well flu, rotavirus and RSV prevention products work.
Ranked for statewide reach and partial plan fit (Grants.gov lists no award amount), supporting the state's manufactured-food safety program standards and its compliance and enforcement work.
Ranked for statewide reach with a $1M award for regional technical assistance that helps health centers expand nutrition services that prevent and manage disease.
Ranked for statewide reach with a $1M award to train clinicians and disease intervention specialists to diagnose, treat and counsel people with or at risk for STIs.
Ranked for high help per person (about $7.86 per NC birth) with a $1M award, funding networks that improve access to maternity and obstetric care in rural areas.
Ranked for statewide reach, providing up to $750K in start-up funding for new accredited rural physician residency programs that address rural doctor shortages.
Ranked for statewide reach and plan fit, a $700K cooperative agreement giving Ryan White recipients the tools and training for integrated HIV prevention and care planning.
Ranked for statewide reach, a $725K implementation-research award testing combined community-clinical strategies to prevent and manage diabetes in health centers and safety-net clinics.
Ranked for statewide reach, $685K to build state occupational safety and health surveillance, a program NIOSH has mostly funded through state health departments.
Ranked for statewide reach, $650K for analysis and technical assistance that helps rural providers succeed in value-based payment and care models.
Ranked for statewide reach, up to $500K for integrated networks of rural hospitals and clinics that address the health needs of targeted rural communities.
Ranked for statewide reach with up to $500K to screen and educate people exposed to radiation from uranium mining and nuclear weapons testing, though few North Carolinians are likely to qualify.
Ranked last in Tier 1 for its small award ($300K), supporting telehealth networks that use nutrition services to prevent and manage chronic disease.

Top ranked in Tier 2 for strong plan fit and a $5M award, placing DHHS on CDC's approved roster for rapid funding when a public health emergency overwhelms state resources; it needs an emergency-management partner.
Ranked for strong plan fit and high help per person (about $17 per NC birth), funding the state Perinatal Quality Collaborative's quality-improvement work for mothers and newborns.
Ranked for the largest Tier 2 award (up to $100M) and high help per child, funding home studies and post-release support for unaccompanied children placed with sponsors.
Ranked for a $6M award, funding research and surveillance on infectious diseases in international travelers to speed outbreak detection; due Nov 5, 2026.
Ranked for its award (up to $5.75M), funding a national center for construction-worker safety research and translation that DHHS would join through a research partner.
Ranked for strong plan fit, about $1M (estimated) to build state capacity in alcohol epidemiology and the prevention of excessive alcohol use.
Ranked for a $4.9M award, funding technical assistance that helps NC's health centers expand preventive and primary care and chronic disease management.
Ranked for its award (about $3.6M, estimated), piloting clinical decision support tools in electronic health records for cervical, breast and colorectal cancer screening.
Earns most of its points from a $5M award, funding an evaluation of rural opioid-response strategies and tools for future community-led rural health initiatives.
Ranked for a $6.75M award and help per child, funding the national resource center that helps states use infant-toddler court teams for young children in the child welfare system.
Ranked for a $5M award and help per child, funding a center that helps home visiting programs use research to improve services and outcomes for families.
Ranked for strong plan fit, up to $500K for rural communities to build networks for substance use disorder prevention, treatment and recovery services.
Ranked for strong plan fit, up to $1.2M to implement and evaluate a comprehensive suicide prevention approach for groups with the highest suicide burden, such as veterans and rural residents.
Ranked for its award (about $2.75M, estimated), raising awareness of hepatitis B and C testing and treatment and building clinicians' skills to treat them.
Ranked for strong plan fit, up to $700K to implement the evidence-based infant-toddler court approach in targeted NC communities.
Ranked for its award (up to $1.4M), funding a Total Worker Health center of excellence that researches safer working conditions and worker well-being.
Ranked for its award (about $1.4M, estimated), funding the state's injury-prevention data, infrastructure and partnerships to prevent unintentional injury.
Ranked for its award (about $2.5M, estimated) and help per person, funding clinic-community collaboratives that integrate HIV care with broader women's health services in the South.
Ranked for statewide reach and plan fit (Grants.gov gives no per-award amount), funding flood mitigation for repeatedly flooded insured buildings, with a 25% match.
Ranked for statewide reach, a $1M award for a network that helps North Carolinians prepare for and stay healthy during international travel; due Nov 5, 2026.
Ranked for statewide reach, $900K for research that helps federal, state and local decision-makers understand health workforce needs.
Ranked for statewide reach, $550K for occupational safety and health training programs, which are mostly run by academic institutions.
Ranked for statewide reach, $450K to implement and evaluate strategies that prevent multiple forms of violence among adolescents and young adults.
Ranked last in Tier 2 because it has no award amount yet, a VA forecast for transitional housing for veterans experiencing homelessness that DHHS would support through a housing partner.

Top ranked in Tier 3 for strong plan fit and a large award (up to $15M), funding statewide early care and education data and technology infrastructure, but its 30% match and required state designation need the secretary.

Ranked for strong plan fit and the highest help per person in Tier 3 (about $382 per NC birth), funding voluntary, evidence-based home visiting for pregnant women and young families, with an award of up to about $48.6M that likely needs an appropriation.
Ranked for a large award (up to $22M), help per person, and funding Title X family planning services statewide, with a required match that the data file missed and that likely needs an appropriation.

Top ranked for DMVA for strong plan fit, the highest help per veteran (about $444), and funding construction and modernization of State Veterans Homes, but needs a 35% state match and an appropriation.

Ranked for strong fit with DMVA's mission, a VA forecast (no award amount yet) for transitional housing with supportive services for veterans experiencing homelessness, which DMVA would need behavioral health and housing partners to deliver.
Ranked for strong plan fit but a small award ($400K), funding research, education and community engagement on the histories of veterans buried in national and state veterans cemeteries.
